evidence.reason: qemu_chr_fe_write's return is accumulated into ibe->outpos with no status check; its residual domain (unchanged by any shown statement) includes -1 on error, so outpos += -1 yields a negative offset that the guard at line 9 (`ibe->outpos < ibe->outlen`, with outlen >= 1 per the line 3 early-out) admits, skipping the reset at lines 15-16; the retry timer at line 11 then re-enters this same statement, which computes `ibe->outbuf + ibe->outpos` (pointer before the array) and `ibe->outlen - ibe->outpos` (inflated length), an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) whose start moves farther before the buffer on each failure (root cause: unchecked security-relevant return, CWE-754). assumptions: On the send path outlen >= 1 because line 3 (`if (ibe->outlen == 0)`) redirects to check_reset, so `outpos < outlen` admits any negative outpos.

The retry timer armed at line 11 re-enters continue_send, matching the function's own send/re-send structure.
limitations: The declared capacity of ibe->outbuf is not shown in the fragment, so the precise extent of the out-of-bounds read cannot be quantified from the shown code; the corrupted offset/length pair and its re-delivery to the sink are nevertheless shown.
